morning.insight:
"역사적인 7월을 넘어 8월로"

지난주 금요일(7/31) 코스피의 17.91% 폭등은 단순한 반등 이상의 의미를 갖습니다. 시츄에이셔널 어웨어니스의 마진콜 정리로 단기 바닥이 확인되었고, 빅테크의 AI CAPEX 확대 발표로 반도체 수요 우려가 일부 해소되었습니다. 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스가 상한가에 육박한 것은 그간 극심했던 저평가를 시장이 인정하기 시작했다는 신호로 읽힙니다.

다만 오늘(월) 차익실현 매물 출회 가능성을 염두에 둬야 합니다. 증권가는 '계단식 점진적 반등'을 전망하며 5,700~6,600선을 예상하고 있습니다. 여전히 美 10년물 금리 4.74%, 중동 전쟁 리스크, 잭슨홀 미팅 등 변수는 산적해 있습니다.

8월의 핵심 이벤트: 잭슨홀 미팅(8/28~29)과 엔비디아 실적(베라 루빈 GPU 언급 여부). 지난달의 공포는 지나갔지만, 달콤한 랠리를 기대하기엔 이릅니다. 하방 5,700선을 지키는지 확인하며 리스크 관리에 집중할 필요가 있습니다.

🎯 오늘 체크할 것: 개장 전 야간선물 동향, 외국인 수급 방향, 전국 폭염 피해 현황

articles.body: 코스피가 7월 31일 하루 1,001.89포인트(17.91%) 폭등하며 사상 최대 상승률 기록. 삼성전자 +26.81%, SK하이닉스 +29.95% 상한가 육박.

articles.headline: 외국인 7조원 순매수…역대급 자금 유입
articles.eng: Foreign investors net buy 7 trillion won…record capital inflow
articles.body: 외국인 투자자들이 7월 31일 하루 7조원 규모 순매수를 기록하며 코스피 폭등 견인. 반도체·AI주 중심 매수세.

articles.headline: 빅테크 AI 투자 확대에 글로벌 기술주 반등
articles.eng: Big Tech AI investment expansion fuels global tech stock rebound
articles.body: 아마존·알파벳·MS·메타 등 빅테크 기업들의 AI 자본지출 확대 발표로 글로벌 기술주 반등. AI 수요 우려 일부 해소.

articles.headline: 증권가 "계단식 점진적 반등…5,700~6,600 예상"
articles.eng: Securities firms predict gradual stair-step rebound…5,700-6,600 range
articles.body: 국내 주요 증권사들이 8월 코스피 5,700~6,600 박스권 전망 제시. 잭슨홀 미팅(8/28~29)과 엔비디아 실적 발표를 핵심 변수로 지목.

articles.headline: 단일종목 레버리지 ETF, 변동성 주범으로 규제 검토
articles.eng: Single-stock leveraged ETFs targeted for regulation as volatility culprit
articles.body: 금융당국이 코스피 급등락의 주요 원인으로 단일종목 레버리지 ETF를 지목, 규제 대책 마련 착수. 투자자 보호 강화 방안 포함.

articles.headline: 반도체 '몰빵' 서학개미…두 달 새 평가액 65조원 증발
articles.eng: Korean retail investors all-in on semiconductors…65 trillion won evaporated in two months
articles.body: 미국 증시에 상장된 반도체주에 집중 투자한 서학개미들의 평가액이 두 달 새 65조원 증발. 환손실과 주가 하락의 이중고. 그럼에도 지난달 7조원 추가 매수.

articles.headline: 삼성전자 26.81% 폭등…262,500원 마감, 상한가 육박
articles.eng: Samsung Electronics surges 26.81%…closes at 262,500 won, near daily limit
articles.body: 삼성전자가 7월 31일 26.81% 급등하며 262,500원에 마감. 외국인과 기관 쌍끌이 매수. AI 반도체 수요 기대감 반영.

articles.headline: SK하이닉스 29.95% 폭등…1,718,000원, 상한가 근접
articles.eng: SK Hynix surges 29.95%…1,718,000 won, near daily limit up
articles.body: SK하이닉스가 29.95% 폭등하며 상한가에 근접. HBM 수요 지속과 AI 투자 확대 기대감에 외국인 매수세 집중.

articles.headline: FOMC 금리 동결에도 美 증시 상승…잭슨홀 주목
articles.eng: US stocks rise despite FOMC rate hold…Jackson Hole in focus
articles.body: 연준이 7월 FOMC에서 금리를 3.75%로 동결했으나 빅테크 실적 호조에 뉴욕 증시 상승 마감. 8월 잭슨홀 미팅에서의 금리 신호에 관심 집중.

articles.headline: Apple Falls, But Amazon, Other Stocks Push Nasdaq Composite Higher
articles.body: U.S. stocks finished higher on the final day of July, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 1.0% as Amazon's 15% surge offset Apple's 7% decline. Big Tech AI spending plans boosted sentiment.

articles.headline: Treasury Yields Rise in Month That Saw Inflation Fears Revive
articles.body: U.S. Treasury yields climbed with the 10-year reaching 4.74%, the highest since January 2025, as inflation fears revived amid Iran war disruptions and resilient economic data.

articles.headline: Oil Jumps 4% as Middle East Tensions Flare, Trump Issues Iran Ultimatum
articles.body: Crude oil surged 3.84% to $86.80 as President Trump threatened Iran with military action while simultaneously offering to cancel strikes if a rapid deal is reached.

articles.headline: South Korea's Kospi Soars Record 18% in Historic Rebound From AI Rout
articles.body: South Korea's Kospi index surged nearly 18% in its largest single-day gain ever, recovering sharply from a brutal July selloff. Samsung and SK Hynix led the rebound as foreign investors poured in a record 7 trillion won.

articles.headline: Big Tech Earnings Show AI Spending Boom Is Still Going Strong
articles.body: Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Meta all reaffirmed massive AI capital expenditure plans for 2026, calming fears that the AI investment cycle was peaking. Combined capex expected to exceed $300 billion.

articles.headline: Nikkei Jumps 4% as Yen Weakens, US-Japan Currency Intervention Looms
articles.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 surged 4.03% to 64,362 as the yen weakened past 157 per dollar. Treasury Secretary Bessent's memo revealed plans for $5-10 billion yen purchase intervention.

articles.headline: Iran War Leaves Economy Facing More Stubborn Inflation, Economists Warn
articles.body: The WSJ survey of economists shows inflation expectations rising as the Iran conflict disrupts supply chains and energy markets. Recession probability lowered but price pressures persist.

articles.headline: Apple's 7% Plunge: Services Miss and Chip Shortages Dent iPhone Maker
articles.body: Apple shares fell 7.35% after reporting services revenue below consensus and warning of production delays due to chip shortages. The decline was the worst among Big Tech on the day.

articles.headline: Trump Gaza Deal: Hamas Disarms, Israel Withdraws — But Neither Wants to Go First
articles.body: President Trump touted a historic agreement for Gaza but significant obstacles remain as neither Hamas nor Israel wants to make the first move in disarmament and withdrawal.

articles.headline: Crushed by Kospi Rout, Angry Koreans Rip Lee and Vow Not to Buy
articles.body: After the historic Kospi crash and subsequent record rebound, angry Korean retail investors are blaming President Lee Jae-myung's policies. Many vow to exit the stock market entirely.

articles.headline: Trump Says US to Cancel Iran Attack Subject to a Rapid Deal
articles.body: President Trump announced the US would cancel planned strikes on Iran contingent on a rapid diplomatic deal, following a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

articles.headline: South Korea Issues Heat Wave Alert as Temperature Hits Record
articles.body: South Korea raised its heat wave alert to the highest level as temperatures approached 40°C across the country. Yangsan recorded five consecutive days above 40°C.

articles.headline: AI Isn't a Catch-All Trade for Stocks in This Earnings Season
articles.body: Bloomberg analysis shows AI exposure is no longer a guaranteed winner this earnings season. Amazon surged 15% on cloud strength while Apple fell 7% despite AI initiatives, showing divergence.

articles.headline: Exxon, Chevron Warn Fuel Prices to Endure as War Knocks Refining
articles.body: Exxon and Chevron warned that elevated fuel prices will persist as the Iran war continues to disrupt refining capacity in the Middle East, with global gasoline and diesel markets tight.

articles.headline: Japan, US Coordinating to Curb Yen Weakness, Katayama Says
articles.body: Japan's Finance Minister Katayama confirmed the US and Japan are coordinating to curb yen weakness, with combined intervention estimated at over 10 trillion yen in recent days.

articles.headline: Warsh's Silent Treatment Has S&P Traders Bracing for Wild Swings
articles.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish post-FOMC silence is keeping traders on edge. S&P 500 options pricing suggests expectations of continued wild swings into August.

articles.headline: Apple Is Reinventing Itself as the World's Biggest Subscription Provider
articles.body: Despite the 7% stock drop, Apple is pivoting aggressively to subscription services, aiming to become the world's largest subscription provider. MacBook Air faces shortages from chip constraints.

articles.headline: AstraZeneca Holds Talks with Bristol Myers Squibb Over $400bn Tie-Up
articles.body: AstraZeneca is in talks with Bristol Myers Squibb over a potential $400 billion merger that would create the world's largest pharmaceutical company by revenue.

articles.headline: Trump's Arctic Mining Deal Signals a New Era of State Capitalism
articles.body: The federal government granted a permit to build a road through Alaskan wilderness in exchange for a stake in a mining company, signaling a new era of state capitalism under Trump.

articles.headline: Phoenix Extends Record-Breaking Heat as West Faces Fire Threat
articles.body: Phoenix extended its record-breaking heat streak as the western US faces extreme fire threats. Climate-driven extreme weather patterns affecting both North America and Asia simultaneously.

articles.headline: Progress Toward Deal Led Trump to Call Off Strikes on Iran
articles.body: Diplomatic progress toward a deal led President Trump to call off planned strikes on Iran, according to administration officials. Saudi Crown Prince MBS played a key mediating role.

articles.headline: Corporate Deals Under Trump Gaza Plan Face Nuclear Energy Hurdles
articles.body: President Trump's Gaza reconstruction plan faces hurdles as corporate deals involving nuclear energy development encounter regulatory and security obstacles in the region.

articles.headline: Wildfires Destroy Hundreds of Buildings as Thousands Evacuate Across West
articles.body: Wildfires are destroying hundreds of buildings across the western United States as thousands evacuate. Extreme heat and drought conditions are fueling the blazes.

articles.headline: South Korea's Kospi Posts Largest-Ever Gain After July's Historic Rout
articles.body: South Korea's Kospi index posted its largest single-day gain in history, surging nearly 18% on July 31, as the market rebounded from its worst month since the global financial crisis.

articles.headline: Iran-Linked Cyberattacks Target U.S. Water Systems Across Multiple States
articles.body: At least seven states have reported cyberattacks on water systems as spy agencies suspect Tehran is targeting critical U.S. infrastructure in retaliation for military strikes.

articles.headline: A Democratic Socialist in the White House? Activists Are Already Eyeing 2028
articles.body: The Democratic Socialists of America summit was abuzz about whether to endorse a presidential candidate for 2028, potentially Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. The movement sees growing momentum.

articles.headline: Big Tech Earnings: Amazon Surges, Apple Stumbles in Divergent AI Paths
articles.body: Amazon's cloud business drove a 15% stock surge while Apple fell 7% on services revenue miss, highlighting diverging fortunes in Big Tech's AI monetization race.

articles.headline: Zelensky Says Ukraine Has 'No Interceptors' as Ballistic Missiles Hit Kyiv
articles.body: Ukrainian President Zelensky warned that Ukraine has run out of air defense interceptors as Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv. He renewed appeals for Patriot systems.

articles.headline: Migrants Overrun Spanish Outpost, Stirring European Outrage
articles.body: Roughly 49,000 migrants rushed into the Spanish territory of Ceuta in 24 hours, sparking European outrage and White House condemnation of Spain as weak on immigration.

articles.headline: Powerful Earthquake Strikes Southern Japan; Dozens Reported Missing
articles.body: A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Japan's Kyushu island with reports of at least one fatality. Nearly 50,000 homes were left without power and dozens remain missing.

articles.headline: Trump Cancels Iran Attack Citing Progress Toward Deal as Israel on Alert
articles.body: President Trump cancelled planned strikes on Iran, citing progress toward a diplomatic deal. Israel remains on high alert as the region watches for the next move.

articles.headline: At Least 7 States Report Cyberattacks as Spy Agencies Suspect Tehran Is Targeting Water
articles.body: Multiple states reported cyberattacks on water infrastructure as U.S. intelligence agencies suspect Iran is behind the coordinated assault on critical civilian systems.

articles.headline: A Democratic Socialist in the White House? Activists Are Thinking Big
articles.body: The Democratic Socialists of America convention saw growing enthusiasm for a 2028 presidential run, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez emerging as a potential standard-bearer for the movement.

articles.headline: Houthis Open Dangerous New Front: Blockade of Saudi Vessels in Red Sea
articles.body: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels opened a dangerous new front by blockading Saudi vessels, adding the Red Sea to the region's growing list of security flashpoints.

articles.headline: U.S. General Warns Pentagon He Lacks Sufficient Forces to Protect Israel
articles.body: A shortage of Navy destroyers used to defend against Iranian ballistic missiles will force the head of U.S. European Command to prioritize homeland defense over Israel, officials said.

articles.headline: Trump Insists Vandals Damaged Reflecting Pool, Blasts DOJ for Dropped Charge
articles.body: President Trump insisted vandals deliberately damaged the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and blasted the Justice Department for dropping felony charges against an Olympic canoeist.

articles.headline: Fauci's Critics Have Power — They're Coming After His Pandemic Record
articles.body: With Republican control of Congress, Dr. Anthony Fauci's critics are intensifying investigations into his pandemic record, with new hearings and document demands.

articles.headline: Chipotle Takes a Daring Gamble: Selling Mexican Food in Mexico
articles.body: The U.S. fast-food chain is betting it can succeed south of the border where Taco Bell has failed twice. Some Mexican customers are embracing it — as American cuisine.

articles.headline: After Months on Iran War's Sidelines, Yemen's Houthis Widen the Conflict
articles.body: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia add another crucial waterway to the region's security concerns. The Red Sea blockade threatens global shipping and oil transport routes.

articles.headline: Trump Blames Minnesota, Not Iran, for Cyberattack on Water Systems
articles.body: At a Camp David Cabinet meeting, President Trump blamed Minnesota's government rather than Iran for cyberattacks on water systems, saying 'I blame it on Minnesota because they're grossly incompetent.'

articles.headline: South Korean Stock Market Soars 18% as Investors Pile Back Into AI
articles.body: South Korea's Kospi surged nearly 18% in a single session as investors rushed back into AI-related stocks following Big Tech's reaffirmation of massive capital expenditure plans for 2026.

articles.headline: AstraZeneca Holds Talks with Bristol Myers Squibb Over $400bn Tie-Up
articles.body: AstraZeneca is in discussions with Bristol Myers Squibb over a potential $400 billion merger that would create the world's largest pharmaceutical group by sales.

articles.headline: America's Biggest Companies Report 'Rock Solid' Profits as Consumers Face Higher Costs
articles.body: S&P 500 companies are on track for their strongest earnings in five years, but consumers face higher costs from inflation and the Iran war's impact on energy and supply chains.

articles.headline: Japan's Yen Jumps 3% as Speculation Over Intervention Swirls
articles.body: The yen surged 3% against the dollar as speculation intensified over coordinated US-Japan currency intervention. Bessent memo revealed plans for massive yen purchases.

articles.headline: Amazon Completes $50bn Investment in OpenAI
articles.body: Amazon has completed a landmark $50 billion investment in OpenAI, deepening the cloud giant's commitment to artificial intelligence and challenging Microsoft's dominance in the sector.

articles.headline: Morgan Stanley's IPO After-Party: A Wealth Management Bonanza
articles.body: Morgan Stanley's successful IPO has triggered a wealth management bonanza as the firm leverages its expanded capital base to capture a growing share of high-net-worth clients.

articles.headline: Citadel's Swoop on Situational Awareness Helped Stem a $3tn AI Rout
articles.body: Citadel's strategic acquisition of Situational Awareness helped stem a $3 trillion AI stock rout, demonstrating how hedge funds are reshaping market dynamics during periods of extreme volatility.

articles.headline: German Carmakers Flood Jobs Market with Managers After Wielding Axe
articles.body: German automakers are flooding the jobs market with experienced managers after extensive restructuring and layoffs, creating opportunities for competitors and startups.

articles.headline: Italy's Giorgia Meloni Bets Big on Nuclear Power Revival
articles.body: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is betting big on a nuclear power revival, pushing for new reactor construction as energy security concerns mount amid the Iran war and gas supply disruptions.

articles.headline: Monte dei Paschi Explores Banco BPM Takeover After Merger Talks Collapse
articles.body: Italy's Monte dei Paschi is exploring a takeover of Banco BPM after 'merger of equals' talks collapsed. The MPS chief executive is weighing an approach to BPM's largest shareholder, Crédit Agricole.

articles.headline: Foreign Bidders Woo UK Companies with 'Bear Hug' Takeover Offers
articles.body: Foreign acquirers are increasingly using 'bear hug' offers — unsolicited but generous bids — to woo UK companies, taking advantage of sterling weakness and depressed London valuations.
